source_fields.formulation: The learner chooses a subset each round against i.i.d. submodular losses whose mean has a unique optimal subset and a positive gap. After acting, the learner may query the current loss function at any subset. The objective is cumulative excess mean loss, and the gap is not disclosed.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: An action is any subset of the ground set $[d]$. Random loss functions $f_t:2^{[d]}\to[0,1]$ are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal D$, and each sample function is submodular. The mean function has a unique minimizing subset: $$\bar f(X)=\mathbb E_{f\sim\mathcal D}f(X),\qquad X^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{X\subseteq[d]}\bar f(X),$$ $$\Delta=\min_{X\ne X^\star}\bigl(\bar f(X)-\bar f(X^\star)\bigr)>0.$$

operations.query_signature: Draw the current function independently. Choose $X_t$, incur $f_t(X_t)$, and then receive feedback. After acting, any subset $X$ may be queried against the same $f_t(X)$, providing full value-oracle access. Randomness comes from function sampling, without additional value noise. The distribution $\mathcal D$, gap $\Delta$, and optimal subset $X^\star$ are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

The source algorithm evaluates $d+1$ subsets per round, giving $N=(d+1)T$ total value queries. Full-feedback permission and actual queries are recorded separately. $$\text{computation per round}=O\!\left(d\,\mathsf{EO}\log d\right).$$ Here $\mathsf{EO}$ is the cost of one set-function evaluation, retaining the stated computational model. Exploration, initialization, and identification are charged; oracle calls, arithmetic, communication, and memory remain separate, without an optimality claim for arithmetic or bits.
